title: Select All Employees
description:
**Goal:** Retrieve the complete roster of company staff.
**Requirements:**
- Return every column and every row from the `employees` table.
**Output Columns:** `emp_id`, `name`, `dept_id`, `salary`, `hire_date`, `manager_id`
expected_query: SELECT * FROM employees;
hints: Use SELECT * to fetch all columns.

title: Employee Names and Salaries
description:
**Goal:** List each employee alongside their compensation.
**Requirements:**
- Fetch the employee name and salary for every record in `employees`.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `salary`
expected_query: SELECT name, salary FROM employees;
hints: Specify 'name, salary' in your SELECT clause.

title: Unique Department Locations
description:
**Goal:** Find all unique office locations across departments.
**Requirements:**
- Return distinct location values from `departments` without duplicates.
**Output Columns:** `location`
expected_query: SELECT DISTINCT location FROM departments;
hints: Use DISTINCT to remove duplicate locations.

title: Product Catalog Details
description:
**Goal:** Display a concise product catalog.
**Requirements:**
- Retrieve product name, category, and unit price for every item in `products`.
**Output Columns:** `product_name`, `category`, `price`
expected_query: SELECT product_name, category, price FROM products;
hints: List the three requested column names in the SELECT clause.

title: Customer City List
description:
**Goal:** Identify all unique cities where customers reside.
**Requirements:**
- Return deduplicated city names from the `customers` table.
**Output Columns:** `city`
expected_query: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers;
hints: Use DISTINCT to get unique city names.

title: Song Catalog
description:
**Goal:** Generate a track listing with playback lengths.
**Requirements:**
- Return title, artist, and duration in seconds for every track in `songs`.
**Output Columns:** `title`, `artist`, `duration_sec`
expected_query: SELECT title, artist, duration_sec FROM songs;
hints: Select the title, artist, and duration_sec columns.

title: Student Majors
description:
**Goal:** List every academic discipline represented by enrolled students.
**Requirements:**
- Return unique major names from `students` without repetition.
**Output Columns:** `major`
expected_query: SELECT DISTINCT major FROM students;

title: Bank Account Types
description:
**Goal:** Enumerate all distinct bank account classifications.
**Requirements:**
- Return unique account type labels from `accounts`.
**Output Columns:** `account_type`
expected_query: SELECT DISTINCT account_type FROM accounts;

title: Formatted Employee Tag
description:
**Goal:** Project a 10% compensation increase for every employee.
**Requirements:**
- For each row in `employees`, compute `annual_compensation` as 110% of `salary`, rounded to 2 decimal places.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `annual_compensation`
expected_query: SELECT name, ROUND(salary * 1.10, 2) AS annual_compensation FROM employees;
hints: Multiply salary by 1.10 and use ROUND(..., 2).

title: Product Discounted Price
description:
**Goal:** Calculate promotional 15%-off catalog pricing.
**Requirements:**
- List each product's name, original `price`, and discounted `sale_price` (85% of `price`), rounded to 2 decimal places.
**Output Columns:** `product_name`, `price`, `sale_price`
expected_query: SELECT product_name, price, ROUND(price * 0.85, 2) AS sale_price FROM products;

title: Song Duration in Minutes
description:
**Goal:** Convert track durations from seconds into minutes.
**Requirements:**
- From `songs`, compute `duration_min` by dividing `duration_sec` by `60.0`, rounded to 2 decimal places.
**Output Columns:** `title`, `artist`, `duration_min`
expected_query: SELECT title, artist, ROUND(duration_sec / 60.0, 2) AS duration_min FROM songs;
hints: Divide duration_sec by 60.0 to prevent integer truncation.

title: Customer Geographic Profile
description:
**Goal:** Build a formatted city-country label for each customer.
**Requirements:**
- Combine `city` and `country` from `customers` into `location` separated by a comma and space (for example, `'Austin, USA'`).
**Output Columns:** `name`, `location`
expected_query: SELECT name, city || ', ' || country AS location FROM customers;

title: Account Liquidity Classification
description:
**Goal:** Classify bank accounts into liquidity tiers.
**Requirements:**
- Assign `tier` for each row in `accounts` in priority order:
  - `'High'` if `balance` is `10000` or greater
  - `'Medium'` if `balance` is `2000` or greater
  - `'Low'` otherwise
**Output Columns:** `account_id`, `balance`, `tier`
expected_query: SELECT account_id, balance, CASE WHEN balance >= 10000 THEN 'High' WHEN balance >= 2000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS tier FROM accounts;

title: Student Standing Category
description:
**Goal:** Assign an academic standing label based on GPA.
**Requirements:**
- Assign `academic_standing` for each row in `students` in priority order:
  - `'Honor Roll'` when `gpa` is at least `3.7`
  - `'Good Standing'` when `gpa` is at least `3.0`
  - `'Needs Improvement'` otherwise
**Output Columns:** `name`, `gpa`, `academic_standing`
expected_query: SELECT name, gpa, CASE WHEN gpa >= 3.7 THEN 'Honor Roll' WHEN gpa >= 3.0 THEN 'Good Standing' ELSE 'Needs Improvement' END AS academic_standing FROM students;
hints: Use CASE WHEN based on gpa.

title: Upper Case Department and Length
description:
**Goal:** Standardize department names to uppercase and measure their string length.
**Requirements:**
- Transform each `dept_name` in `departments` to uppercase as `department_upper` and compute its character count as `name_length`.
**Output Columns:** `department_upper`, `name_length`
expected_query: SELECT UPPER(dept_name) AS department_upper, LENGTH(dept_name) AS name_length FROM departments;

title: Order Status Formatter
description:
**Goal:** Map raw order statuses to operational action labels.
**Requirements:**
- Assign `status_label` for each order in `orders`:
  - `'Urgent'` when `status` is `'Shipped'`
  - `'Complete'` when `status` is `'Delivered'`
  - `'Review'` for all other statuses
**Output Columns:** `order_id`, `total_amount`, `status_label`
expected_query: SELECT order_id, total_amount, CASE status WHEN 'Shipped' THEN 'Urgent' WHEN 'Delivered' THEN 'Complete' ELSE 'Review' END AS status_label FROM orders;

title: Multi-Tiered Salary Equity Index
description:
**Goal:** Categorize staff into compensation equity bands using salary and reporting structure.
**Requirements:**
- Evaluate each employee in `employees` using `equity_band` in strict top-to-bottom priority:
  - `'Executive'` if `salary` is at least `90000` and they have no manager (`manager_id` is null)
  - `'Senior Lead'` if `salary` is at least `80000`
  - `'Specialist'` if `salary` is at least `65000`
  - `'Associate'` otherwise
**Output Columns:** `emp_id`, `name`, `salary`, `equity_band`
expected_query: SELECT emp_id, name, salary, CASE WHEN salary >= 90000 AND manager_id IS NULL THEN 'Executive' WHEN salary >= 80000 THEN 'Senior Lead' WHEN salary >= 65000 THEN 'Specialist' ELSE 'Associate' END AS equity_band FROM employees;
hints: Order your CASE conditions from most specific to least.

title: Inventory Valuation Risk Matrix
description:
**Goal:** Assess capital tied up in product inventory and tag capital risk.
**Requirements:**
- For each item in `products`, compute `inventory_value` as unit price multiplied by available stock.
- Assign `risk_rating` based on `inventory_value`:
  - `'Critical Capital'` if strictly greater than `5000`
  - `'Moderate'` if at least `1000`
  - `'Low'` otherwise
**Output Columns:** `product_id`, `product_name`, `inventory_value`, `risk_rating`
expected_query: SELECT product_id, product_name, price * stock AS inventory_value, CASE WHEN price * stock > 5000 THEN 'Critical Capital' WHEN price * stock >= 1000 THEN 'Moderate' ELSE 'Low' END AS risk_rating FROM products;
hints: Compute price * stock in CASE conditions.

title: Transaction Fraud Risk Flagging
description:
**Goal:** Flag banking transactions by withdrawal size and processing outcome.
**Requirements:**
- Evaluate each record in `transactions` using `risk_flag` in strict priority order:
  - `'High Risk'` if `amount` is strictly over `2000` and `txn_type` is `'Withdrawal'`
  - `'Suspicious'` if `status` is `'Failed'`
  - `'Normal'` otherwise
**Output Columns:** `txn_id`, `account_id`, `amount`, `risk_flag`
expected_query: SELECT txn_id, account_id, amount, CASE WHEN amount > 2000 AND txn_type = 'Withdrawal' THEN 'High Risk' WHEN status = 'Failed' THEN 'Suspicious' ELSE 'Normal' END AS risk_flag FROM transactions;

title: Song Era and Length Categorization
description:
**Goal:** Classify songs by release era and track length.
**Requirements:**
- Assign `category` for each track in `songs` in priority order:
  - `'Modern Epic'` if `release_year` is `2022` or later and `duration_sec` is over `220`
  - `'Classic Short'` if `release_year` is before `2021` and `duration_sec` is `210` or less
  - `'Standard'` otherwise
**Output Columns:** `title`, `artist`, `category`
expected_query: SELECT title, artist, CASE WHEN release_year >= 2022 AND duration_sec > 220 THEN 'Modern Epic' WHEN release_year < 2021 AND duration_sec <= 210 THEN 'Classic Short' ELSE 'Standard' END AS category FROM songs;
hints: Combine release_year and duration_sec in CASE conditions.

title: Employees with High Salary
description:
**Goal:** Find high-earning employees across the company.
**Requirements:**
- Return full records from `employees` for staff whose `salary` is strictly greater than `80000`.
**Output Columns:** `emp_id`, `name`, `dept_id`, `salary`, `hire_date`, `manager_id`
expected_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 80000;

title: Engineering Department Staff
description:
**Goal:** List names and pay for staff in department `1`.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `employees` to records where `dept_id` equals `1`.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `salary`
expected_query: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1;

title: Delivered Customer Orders
description:
**Goal:** Inspect all orders that have already been delivered.
**Requirements:**
- Return every column from `orders` for rows whose `status` is `'Delivered'`.
**Output Columns:** `order_id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `status`, `total_amount`
expected_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'Delivered';

title: Low Stock Products Alert
description:
**Goal:** Identify products running low on inventory.
**Requirements:**
- Find products in `products` with `stock` of `25` units or fewer.
**Output Columns:** `product_name`, `stock`
expected_query: SELECT product_name, stock FROM products WHERE stock <= 25;

title: Premium Streaming Subscribers
description:
**Goal:** Retrieve all Premium-tier music streaming users.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `users` to accounts whose `plan` is `'Premium'`.
**Output Columns:** `username`, `signup_date`
expected_query: SELECT username, signup_date FROM users WHERE plan = 'Premium';

title: Long Duration Tracks
description:
**Goal:** Find longer tracks in the music catalog.
**Requirements:**
- Retrieve songs from `songs` whose `duration_sec` is at least `240` seconds.
**Output Columns:** `title`, `artist`
expected_query: SELECT title, artist FROM songs WHERE duration_sec >= 240;

title: Computer Science Undergrads
description:
**Goal:** List students majoring in Computer Science.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `students` to rows with `major` equal to `'Computer Science'`.
**Output Columns:** `student_id`, `name`, `gpa`
expected_query: SELECT student_id, name, gpa FROM students WHERE major = 'Computer Science';

title: Substantial Account Balances
description:
**Goal:** Locate bank accounts holding substantial balances.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `accounts` to rows with a `balance` strictly above `5000`.
**Output Columns:** `account_id`, `balance`
expected_query: SELECT account_id, balance FROM accounts WHERE balance > 5000;

title: Employees in Mid-Level Range Without Managers
description:
**Goal:** Find autonomous mid-band earners with no listed manager.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `employees` to staff whose `salary` is between `60000` and `90000` inclusive and whose `manager_id` is null.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `salary`
expected_query: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 60000 AND 90000 AND manager_id IS NULL;

title: Recent Hires in Engineering or HR
description:
**Goal:** Identify newer hires in departments `1` and `4`.
**Requirements:**
- Include employees hired on or after `'2022-01-01'` whose `dept_id` is either `1` or `4`.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `hire_date`
expected_query: SELECT name, hire_date FROM employees WHERE hire_date >= '2022-01-01' AND dept_id IN (1, 4);

title: High Value Delivered or Shipped Orders
description:
**Goal:** Audit high-value fulfilled or in-transit orders.
**Requirements:**
- Return orders from `orders` whose `status` is `'Delivered'` or `'Shipped'` and `total_amount` is at least `100`.
**Output Columns:** `order_id`, `total_amount`
expected_query: SELECT order_id, total_amount FROM orders WHERE status IN ('Delivered', 'Shipped') AND total_amount >= 100;

title: Electronics Above Average Threshold
description:
**Goal:** Find mid-priced Electronics inventory.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `products` to category `'Electronics'` with `price` from `50` through `1000` inclusive.
**Output Columns:** `product_name`, `price`
expected_query: SELECT product_name, price FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics' AND price BETWEEN 50 AND 1000;

title: Electronic Songs by Neon Pulse
description:
**Goal:** Locate longer Electronic songs by Neon Pulse.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `songs` to artist `'Neon Pulse'`, genre `'Electronic'`, and `duration_sec` strictly greater than `200`.
**Output Columns:** `title`, `duration_sec`
expected_query: SELECT title, duration_sec FROM songs WHERE artist = 'Neon Pulse' AND genre = 'Electronic' AND duration_sec > 200;
hints: Filter on artist, genre, and duration

title: Students with High GPA in Modern Cohorts
description:
**Goal:** Highlight high-achieving students from recent admission cohorts.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `students` to `gpa` at least `3.5` and `admission_year` `2021` or later.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `gpa`
expected_query: SELECT name, gpa FROM students WHERE gpa >= 3.5 AND admission_year >= 2021;

title: High Volume Completed Withdrawals
description:
**Goal:** Track sizeable completed withdrawal transactions.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `transactions` to `txn_type` `'Withdrawal'`, `status` `'Completed'`, and `amount` at least `300`.
**Output Columns:** `txn_id`, `amount`, `txn_date`
expected_query: SELECT txn_id, amount, txn_date FROM transactions WHERE txn_type = 'Withdrawal' AND status = 'Completed' AND amount >= 300;

title: Unassigned Department Employees
description:
**Goal:** Find employees who either lack a department or earn below the base band.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `employees` to records where `dept_id` is missing (null) OR `salary` is strictly under `60000`.
**Output Columns:** `emp_id`, `name`
expected_query: SELECT emp_id, name FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NULL OR salary < 60000;

title: Complex Multilateral Staff Filter
description:
**Goal:** Select staff meeting either senior department `1` pay criteria or tenured department `3` criteria.
**Requirements:**
- Return employees from `employees` matching either:
  - `dept_id` is `1` and `salary` is at least `85000`, OR
  - `dept_id` is `3` and `hire_date` is on or after `'2020-01-01'`.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `salary`, `dept_id`
expected_query: SELECT name, salary, dept_id FROM employees WHERE (dept_id = 1 AND salary >= 85000) OR (dept_id = 3 AND hire_date >= '2020-01-01');

title: Pattern Match and Capital Threshold
description:
**Goal:** Spot flagship `'Pro'` items or high-capital Furniture stock.
**Requirements:**
- Return products matching either:
  - `product_name` contains the substring `'Pro'`, OR
  - `category` is `'Furniture'` and total inventory value (`price * stock`) exceeds `2000`.
**Output Columns:** `product_name`, `price`, `stock`
expected_query: SELECT product_name, price, stock FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%Pro%' OR (category = 'Furniture' AND price * stock > 2000);
hints: Use LIKE and arithmetic in WHERE

title: Strict Fraud Screening Clause
description:
**Goal:** Screen transactions requiring manual compliance review.
**Requirements:**
- Return rows from `transactions` that are either:
  - `'Withdrawal'` transactions with `amount` strictly above `400`, OR
  - Any transaction whose `status` is `'Failed'`.
**Output Columns:** `txn_id`, `account_id`, `amount`
expected_query: SELECT txn_id, account_id, amount FROM transactions WHERE (txn_type = 'Withdrawal' AND amount > 400) OR status = 'Failed';
hints: Group the withdrawal check with OR failed

title: Selective Cohort Honors Query
description:
**Goal:** Identify students qualifying for major-specific honors thresholds.
**Requirements:**
- Return students meeting either criterion:
  - `major` is `'Computer Science'` or `'Physics'` with `gpa` at least `3.6`, OR
  - `major` is `'Mathematics'` with `gpa` strictly above `3.0`.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `major`, `gpa`
expected_query: SELECT name, major, gpa FROM students WHERE (major IN ('Computer Science', 'Physics') AND gpa >= 3.6) OR (major = 'Mathematics' AND gpa > 3.0);
hints: Use IN with combined gpa logic

title: Employee Department Inner Join
description:
**Goal:** Pair each assigned employee with their department name.
**Requirements:**
- Match `employees` and `departments` on matching department IDs (excluding unassigned staff).
**Output Columns:** `employee_name`, `dept_name`
expected_query: SELECT e.name AS employee_name, d.dept_name FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id;

title: Customer Orders Join
description:
**Goal:** Display customer names alongside each order they placed.
**Requirements:**
- Combine `customers` and `orders` by matching customer ID.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `order_id`, `total_amount`
expected_query: SELECT c.name, o.order_id, o.total_amount FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

title: Order Items Product Info
description:
**Goal:** Show product names and quantities for every order line item.
**Requirements:**
- Connect `order_items` to `products` by matching product ID.
**Output Columns:** `order_id`, `product_name`, `quantity`
expected_query: SELECT oi.order_id, p.product_name, oi.quantity FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id;

title: User Play Logs
description:
**Goal:** Produce a log of which user streamed which song.
**Requirements:**
- Link listening records in `plays` with `users` and `songs` to resolve each listener's `username` and song title as `song_title`.
**Output Columns:** `username`, `song_title`
expected_query: SELECT u.username, s.title AS song_title FROM plays p INNER JOIN users u ON p.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN songs s ON p.song_id = s.song_id;
hints: Join plays to users and songs

title: Student Enrollment Course Titles
description:
**Goal:** List enrolled students alongside their course titles.
**Requirements:**
- Connect `enrollments` with `students` and `courses` to pair student names with course titles.
**Output Columns:** `student_name`, `course_title`
expected_query: SELECT s.name AS student_name, c.title AS course_title FROM enrollments e INNER JOIN students s ON e.student_id = s.student_id INNER JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.course_id;
hints: Join enrollments with students and courses

title: Account Transactions List
description:
**Goal:** View banking transactions enriched with account type details.
**Requirements:**
- Combine `accounts` and `transactions` on `account_id`.
**Output Columns:** `account_id`, `account_type`, `amount`, `txn_type`
expected_query: SELECT a.account_id, a.account_type, t.amount, t.txn_type FROM accounts a INNER JOIN transactions t ON a.account_id = t.account_id;

title: Employee Project Hours
description:
**Goal:** Report employee hours logged per project.
**Requirements:**
- Connect `employees`, `emp_projects`, and `projects` to pair employee names with project names and hours worked.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `project_name`, `hours_worked`
expected_query: SELECT e.name, p.project_name, ep.hours_worked FROM employees e INNER JOIN emp_projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id INNER JOIN projects p ON ep.project_id = p.project_id;

title: Department Locations and Staff
description:
**Goal:** Find all employees based in the San Francisco office.
**Requirements:**
- Match `employees` with `departments` and keep only staff whose department `location` is `'San Francisco'`.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `location`
expected_query: SELECT e.name, d.location FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id WHERE d.location = 'San Francisco';

title: Left Join Department Employees Including Unassigned
description:
**Goal:** List every employee and their department, labeling unassigned staff clearly.
**Requirements:**
- Include all rows from `employees`, even those without a department.
- If an employee has no department match, display `'No Department'` as `dept_name`.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `dept_name`
expected_query: SELECT e.name, COALESCE(d.dept_name, 'No Department') AS dept_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id;

title: All Customers with Orders or Null
description:
**Goal:** List every customer alongside any orders they have placed.
**Requirements:**
- Keep all customers from `customers`, including customers who have never placed an order (leaving order fields null).
**Output Columns:** `name`, `order_id`, `total_amount`
expected_query: SELECT c.name, o.order_id, o.total_amount FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

title: Self Join Employee and Manager
description:
**Goal:** Map every employee to the name of their direct manager.
**Requirements:**
- Relate `employees` back to itself via `manager_id` and `emp_id`.
- Keep every employee in the result, leaving `manager` null if they do not report to anyone.
**Output Columns:** `employee`, `manager`
expected_query: SELECT e.name AS employee, m.name AS manager FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id;

title: Multi-Table Order Item Details with Item Subtotal
description:
**Goal:** Compute item-level subtotals per customer across order lines.
**Requirements:**
- Connect `customers`, `orders`, `order_items`, and `products`.
- Rename customer name as `customer` and calculate `subtotal` as `unit_price * quantity`.
**Output Columns:** `customer`, `product_name`, `quantity`, `subtotal`
expected_query: SELECT c.name AS customer, p.product_name, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price * oi.quantity AS subtotal FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id INNER JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id;
hints: Join 4 tables: customers -> orders -> order_items -> products

title: Courses with Enrolled Student Counts
description:
**Goal:** Report enrollment headcounts for every course, including empty ones.
**Requirements:**
- Include every course in `courses` (even courses with zero enrollments).
- Aggregate at the course level (`course_id` and `title`) to return enrolled student counts as `student_count`.
**Output Columns:** `title`, `student_count`
expected_query: SELECT c.title, COUNT(e.student_id) AS student_count FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.title;
hints: LEFT JOIN courses with enrollments and COUNT

title: Total Play Counts per Song
description:
**Goal:** Count total streams for every track in the catalog, including unplayed tracks.
**Requirements:**
- Include every song from `songs`, showing `0` as `play_count` for songs with no rows in `plays`.
- Aggregate per song (`song_id`, `title`, and `artist`).
**Output Columns:** `title`, `artist`, `play_count`
expected_query: SELECT s.title, s.artist, COUNT(p.play_id) AS play_count FROM songs s LEFT JOIN plays p ON s.song_id = p.song_id GROUP BY s.song_id, s.title, s.artist;

title: Department Project Allocation Join
description:
**Goal:** List unique department-project pairings based on employee assignments.
**Requirements:**
- Link `departments`, `employees`, `emp_projects`, and `projects`.
- Deduplicate so each `(dept_name, project_name)` pair appears once.
**Output Columns:** `dept_name`, `project_name`
expected_query: SELECT d.dept_name, p.project_name FROM departments d INNER JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id INNER JOIN emp_projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id INNER JOIN projects p ON ep.project_id = p.project_id GROUP BY d.dept_name, p.project_name;
hints: Join departments through employees to emp_projects and projects

title: Accounts Without Any Transactions
description:
**Goal:** Find bank accounts with zero recorded transaction history.
**Requirements:**
- Return accounts from `accounts` that have no corresponding rows in `transactions`.
**Output Columns:** `account_id`, `account_type`
expected_query: SELECT a.account_id, a.account_type FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON a.account_id = t.account_id WHERE t.txn_id IS NULL;
hints: Use LEFT JOIN and WHERE t.txn_id IS NULL

title: Comprehensive Multi-Layer Manager Department Summary
description:
**Goal:** Build an organizational summary for staff earning `70000` or more.
**Requirements:**
- Include all employees in `employees` whose `salary` is at least `70000`.
- Resolve their manager's name (defaulting to `'Top Level'` when `manager_id` is null) and their department name (retaining null if unassigned).
**Output Columns:** `employee`, `manager`, `dept_name`
expected_query: SELECT e.name AS employee, COALESCE(m.name, 'Top Level') AS manager, d.dept_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id WHERE e.salary >= 70000;
hints: Combine self-join with department left join and filter

title: Customers with Delivered Electronics
description:
**Goal:** Find unique customers who received delivered Electronics items.
**Requirements:**
- Connect customers to ordered products and keep only orders with `status = 'Delivered'` containing a product in category `'Electronics'`.
- Return each qualifying customer name once.
**Output Columns:** `customer_name`
expected_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.name AS customer_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' AND p.category = 'Electronics';
hints: Join 4 tables and apply status and category filters

title: Students Taking Both CS and Math Courses
description:
**Goal:** Identify students enrolled in both Computer Science and Mathematics courses.
**Requirements:**

expected_query: SELECT ROUND(AVG(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity), 2) AS avg_item_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics';

title: Count of Songs Above 200 Seconds per Genre
description:
**Goal:** Count tracks strictly longer than `200` seconds within every genre.
**Requirements:**
- Aggregate all genres in `songs`, returning every genre even if zero tracks exceed `200` seconds (`long_songs_count`).
**Output Columns:** `genre`, `long_songs_count`
expected_query: SELECT genre, COUNT(CASE WHEN duration_sec > 200 THEN 1 END) AS long_songs_count FROM songs GROUP BY genre;

title: Dean's List Student Count per Cohort
description:
**Goal:** Count Dean's List eligible students (`gpa` of `3.6+`) in every admission cohort.
**Requirements:**
- Aggregate `students` by `admission_year`, keeping every cohort year and counting only rows meeting `gpa` of `3.6` or higher as `honors_count`.
**Output Columns:** `admission_year`, `honors_count`
expected_query: SELECT admission_year, COUNT(CASE WHEN gpa >= 3.6 THEN 1 END) AS honors_count FROM students GROUP BY admission_year;

title: Completed Deposit vs Withdrawal Volumes
description:
**Goal:** Compare completed deposit and withdrawal volumes in a single summary row.
**Requirements:**
- Restrict `transactions` to `status = 'Completed'`.
- Return conditionally summed totals for `'Deposit'` (`deposits_sum`) and `'Withdrawal'` (`withdrawals_sum`), defaulting to `0` if none exist.
**Output Columns:** `deposits_sum`, `withdrawals_sum`
expected_query: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'Deposit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS deposits_sum, SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'Withdrawal' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS withdrawals_sum FROM transactions WHERE status = 'Completed';

title: Average Hours Logged per Department Employee
description:
**Goal:** Calculate average project hours logged per department.
**Requirements:**
- Connect `departments`, `employees`, and `emp_projects`, aggregate by `dept_name`, and round the average `hours_worked` to 1 decimal place as `avg_hours`.
**Output Columns:** `dept_name`, `avg_hours`
expected_query: SELECT d.dept_name, ROUND(AVG(ep.hours_worked), 1) AS avg_hours FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id JOIN emp_projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id GROUP BY d.dept_name;

title: Total Value of Inventory in Stock
description:
**Goal:** Calculate total inventory capital tied up in each product category.
**Requirements:**
- Aggregate `products` by `category`, summing `price * stock` as `total_inv_value`.
**Output Columns:** `category`, `total_inv_value`
expected_query: SELECT category, SUM(price * stock) AS total_inv_value FROM products GROUP BY category;

title: Executive Compensation Ratio Matrix
description:
**Goal:** Build a single-row executive compensation dispersion matrix.
**Requirements:**
- Across all `employees`, compute:
  - `salary_ratio`: highest salary divided by lowest salary (using floating-point division), rounded to 2 decimal places
  - `mean_salary`: average salary rounded to 2 decimal places
  - `total_gap`: difference between highest and lowest salary
**Output Columns:** `salary_ratio`, `mean_salary`, `total_gap`
expected_query: SELECT ROUND(MAX(salary) * 1.0 / MIN(salary), 2) AS salary_ratio, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS mean_salary, MAX(salary) - MIN(salary) AS total_gap FROM employees;
hints: Compute ratio of MAX to MIN salary

title: Net Cash Flow Across All Completed Transactions
description:
**Goal:** Compute overall net cash flow across completed banking activity.
**Requirements:**
- Restrict `transactions` to `status = 'Completed'`.
- Add `'Deposit'` amounts, subtract `'Withdrawal'` amounts (treating any other type as `0`), and round the total to 2 decimal places as `net_cash_flow`.
**Output Columns:** `net_cash_flow`
expected_query: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'Deposit' THEN amount WHEN txn_type = 'Withdrawal' THEN -amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS net_cash_flow FROM transactions WHERE status = 'Completed';

title: Customer Conversion and Average Ticket Size
description:
**Goal:** Compute delivered customer reach, order count, and average ticket size.
**Requirements:**
- Combine `customers` with `orders` keeping only `status = 'Delivered'`.
- Return unique customer count (`total_customers`), order count (`total_orders`), and total delivered revenue divided by delivered order count rounded to 2 decimal places (`avg_ticket_size`).
**Output Columns:** `total_customers`, `total_orders`, `avg_ticket_size`
expected_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS total_customers, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, ROUND(SUM(o.total_amount) / COUNT(o.order_id), 2) AS avg_ticket_size FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'Delivered';
hints: Combine distinct customers with average ticket size

title: Comprehensive Academic Performance Summary
description:
**Goal:** Produce a single-row academic performance overview.
**Requirements:**
- Across all `students`, compute total headcount (`total_students`), mean GPA rounded to 2 decimal places (`mean_gpa`), and the highest-minus-lowest GPA spread rounded to 2 decimal places (`gpa_range`).
**Output Columns:** `total_students`, `mean_gpa`, `gpa_range`
expected_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_students, ROUND(AVG(gpa), 2) AS mean_gpa, ROUND(MAX(gpa) - MIN(gpa), 2) AS gpa_range FROM students;

title: Top 3 Highest Paid Employees
description:
**Goal:** Find the 3 highest-paid employees.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `employees` from highest `salary` to lowest and return only the first 3 rows.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `salary`
expected_query: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Top 3 Most Expensive Products
description:
**Goal:** List the 3 most expensive catalog products.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `products` by `price` descending and return only the top 3 rows.
**Output Columns:** `product_name`, `price`
expected_query: SELECT product_name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Top 2 Students by GPA
description:
**Goal:** Identify the top 2 students by GPA.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `students` from highest `gpa` to lowest and return only the first 2 rows.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `gpa`
expected_query: SELECT name, gpa FROM students ORDER BY gpa DESC LIMIT 2;

title: 3 Longest Songs
description:
**Goal:** Find the 3 longest songs in the catalog.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `songs` from longest `duration_sec` to shortest and limit to 3 rows.
**Output Columns:** `title`, `duration_sec`
expected_query: SELECT title, duration_sec FROM songs ORDER BY duration_sec DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Highest Balance Bank Account
description:
**Goal:** Retrieve the single bank account with the largest balance.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `accounts` by `balance` descending and return only the top row.
**Output Columns:** `account_id`, `balance`
expected_query: SELECT account_id, balance FROM accounts ORDER BY balance DESC LIMIT 1;

title: Latest 3 Orders Placed
description:
**Goal:** Inspect the 3 most recent orders.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `orders` by `order_date` descending (newest first) and return 3 rows.
**Output Columns:** `order_id`, `order_date`, `total_amount`
expected_query: SELECT order_id, order_date, total_amount FROM orders ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Oldest 3 Employees by Hire Date
description:
**Goal:** Identify the 3 longest-tenured employees by hire date.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `employees` chronologically by `hire_date` ascending (earliest first) and return 3 rows.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `hire_date`
expected_query: SELECT name, hire_date FROM employees ORDER BY hire_date ASC LIMIT 3;

title: Largest 2 Project Budgets
description:
**Goal:** List the 2 largest project budgets.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `projects` from highest `budget` to lowest and return the top 2 rows.
**Output Columns:** `project_name`, `budget`
expected_query: SELECT project_name, budget FROM projects ORDER BY budget DESC LIMIT 2;

title: Sorted Employees by Department and Salary
description:
**Goal:** Sort assigned staff by department ID and descending salary.
**Requirements:**
- Exclude employees with null `dept_id`.
- Order primarily by `dept_id` ascending, then by `salary` descending.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `dept_id`, `salary`
expected_query: SELECT name, dept_id, salary FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY dept_id ASC, salary DESC;
hints: ORDER BY dept_id ASC, salary DESC

title: Pagination Offset for Products
description:
**Goal:** Return the 3rd, 4th, and 5th most expensive products (paginated slice).
**Requirements:**
- Sort `products` by `price` descending.
- Skip the top 2 rows and return the next 3 rows.
**Output Columns:** `product_name`, `price`
expected_query: SELECT product_name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3 OFFSET 2;

title: Top 3 Customers by Total Spend
description:
**Goal:** Rank and return the top 3 customers by lifetime order spend.
**Requirements:**
- Combine `customers` with `orders`, aggregate spend per customer (`customer_id` and `name`), sort highest `total_spend` first, and return only the top 3.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `total_spend`
expected_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spend FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY total_spend DESC LIMIT 3;
hints: Group by customer, order by total_spend desc limit 3

title: Top 2 Most Streamed Songs
description:
**Goal:** Find the 2 most streamed songs.
**Requirements:**
- Combine `songs` with `plays` and tally stream counts per song (`song_id` and `title`).
- Sort by `play_count` descending (breaking ties alphabetically by `title` ascending) and return the top 2 rows.
**Output Columns:** `title`, `play_count`
expected_query: SELECT s.title, COUNT(p.play_id) AS play_count FROM songs s JOIN plays p ON s.song_id = p.song_id GROUP BY s.song_id, s.title ORDER BY play_count DESC, s.title ASC LIMIT 2;
hints: Order by play_count desc, title asc limit 2

title: Students Ranked by GPA Within Admission Year
description:
**Goal:** Sort students chronologically by cohort year and within each year by top GPA.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `students` primarily by `admission_year` ascending, and secondarily by `gpa` descending.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `admission_year`, `gpa`
expected_query: SELECT name, admission_year, gpa FROM students ORDER BY admission_year ASC, gpa DESC;
hints: ORDER BY admission_year ASC, gpa DESC

title: Largest Completed Transaction Entries
description:
**Goal:** Surface the 3 largest completed banking transactions.
**Requirements:**
- Filter `transactions` to `status = 'Completed'`, sort by `amount` descending, and return the top 3 rows.
**Output Columns:** `txn_id`, `amount`, `txn_date`
expected_query: SELECT txn_id, amount, txn_date FROM transactions WHERE status = 'Completed' ORDER BY amount DESC LIMIT 3;
hints: Filter completed, order by amount desc limit 3

title: Top 3 Products by Inventory Capital Value
description:
**Goal:** Find the top 3 products by total capital value in stock.
**Requirements:**
- Calculate `total_value` as `price * stock` from `products`, sort from highest value to lowest, and return 3 rows.
**Output Columns:** `product_name`, `total_value`
expected_query: SELECT product_name, price * stock AS total_value FROM products ORDER BY total_value DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Departments by Total Headcount Descending
description:
**Goal:** List every department sorted from largest headcount to smallest.
**Requirements:**
- Include every department in `departments`, even departments with `0` employees.
- Sort by `headcount` descending, breaking ties alphabetically by `dept_name` ascending.
**Output Columns:** `dept_name`, `headcount`
expected_query: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS headcount FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_name ORDER BY headcount DESC, d.dept_name ASC;
hints: ORDER BY headcount DESC, dept_name ASC

title: Second Lowest Salary in Company
description:
**Goal:** Retrieve the second-lowest salary in the company.
**Requirements:**
- Sort `employees` by `salary` ascending, skip the single lowest row, and return the next 1 row.
**Output Columns:** `salary`
expected_query: SELECT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary ASC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;
hints: ORDER BY salary ASC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1

title: Top 2 Highest Grossing Product Categories
description:
**Goal:** Identify the 2 highest-grossing product categories.
**Requirements:**
- Combine `products` with `order_items` and total `quantity * unit_price` per `category` as `category_revenue`.
- Sort from highest revenue to lowest and return the top 2 rows.
**Output Columns:** `category`, `category_revenue`
expected_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS category_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY category_revenue DESC LIMIT 2;
hints: Group by category, order by revenue desc limit 2

title: Customer with Second Highest Single Order
description:
**Goal:** Find the customer behind the second-largest single order.
**Requirements:**
- Combine `customers` with `orders`, sort by `total_amount` descending, skip the top 1 order, and return the next 1 row.
**Output Columns:** `name`, `total_amount`
expected_query: SELECT c.name, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.total_amount DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;
hints: Join customers to orders, order by total_amount desc limit 1 offset 1

title: Third Most Active Song Streamer
description:
**Goal:** Identify the third most active music listener.
**Requirements:**
- Combine `users` with `plays` and tally streams per user (`user_id` and `username`).
- Sort by `play_count` descending (breaking ties alphabetically by `username` ascending), skip the top 2 users, and return the 3rd user.
**Output Columns:** `username`, `play_count`
expected_query: SELECT u.username, COUNT(p.play_id) AS play_count FROM users u JOIN plays p ON u.user_id = p.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.username ORDER BY play_count DESC, u.username ASC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2;
hints: ORDER BY play_count DESC, username ASC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2
